executive_summary: Today's intelligence picture is dominated by a single accelerating theme: artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming both a weapon and a shield across every domain of national security, from industrial control systems and military platforms to geopolitical influence operations and domestic surveillance. The convergence of the White House AI security strategy, Congressional hearings on critical infrastructure, the Trump administration's push to integrate AI across national security agencies, and simultaneous moves by Russia to upgrade surveillance capabilities and China to expand AI influence in Africa and Latin America signals that great power competition is increasingly being contested in the cognitive and digital layers rather than exclusively on traditional battlefields. Active threats remain acute in the near term, with CISA flagging exploited vulnerabilities including an AI platform flaw, a major healthcare data breach, and an insider threat case involving ISIS financing all pointing to a persistent and diversified attack surface against US interests. The fragile Iran-Israel pause and the Navy strike on an oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman serve as reminders that kinetic escalation risk has not receded, and any deterioration in that theater would compound stress on supply chains and critical infrastructure already identified as vulnerable to detection evasion and cyberattack.

sections.title: Cyber
sections.intro: Today's cyber landscape shows continued vulnerability exploitation, regulatory enforcement actions, and state-level digital surveillance expansion.

items.headline: DentaQuest Breach Exposes 2.6 Million Dental Benefits Records
items.summary: ShinyHunters threat group leaked data from DentaQuest, a major U.S. dental benefits administrator owned by Sun Life, affecting 2.6 million accounts including names and emails. The incident highlights ongoing risks to healthcare sector data and the persistence of established cybercriminal groups in targeting high-value datasets. This breach adds to growing concerns about healthcare data protection amid increasing digitization.

items.headline: CISA Flags Two Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities Including AI Platform Flaw
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-42271 affecting BerriAI LiteLLM and CVE-2026-50751 in Check Point Security Gateway to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog based on confirmed active exploitation. The inclusion of an AI platform vulnerability signals expanding attack surfaces as organizations integrate AI tools. Federal agencies now have binding deadlines to patch these flaws.

items.headline: WhatsApp Seeks Contempt Order Against NSO for Violating Spyware Injunction
items.summary: WhatsApp filed a federal contempt motion alleging NSO Group violated a permanent court injunction by conducting new spearphishing attacks against its users. This escalation in the long-running legal battle could result in additional penalties for the Israeli spyware firm and sets precedent for enforcing court orders against surveillance technology companies. The case tests judicial oversight of commercial spyware operations.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: Russia Updates SORM Digital Surveillance System for Enhanced Citizen Monitoring
items.summary: Russia's Ministry of Digital Development published new technical standards for its SORM surveillance system, upgrading capabilities to track citizens' online activities more comprehensively. The regulatory changes reflect Russia's continued expansion of domestic digital monitoring infrastructure amid geopolitical tensions. These updates may influence global discussions about state surveillance boundaries and digital rights.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

sections.title: Geopolitical
sections.intro: Global tensions simmer as Iran-Israel hostilities pause precariously, China expands digital influence in Africa, and complex supply chains challenge traditional security approaches.

items.headline: Iran-Israel War Reaches Fragile Pause After Escalating Attacks
items.summary: Iran and Israel have stepped back from the brink following recent military exchanges, but the ceasefire remains extremely fragile with another Israeli assault on Beirut potentially collapsing the truce entirely. Trump's attempt to end the conflict faces resistance from all parties involved, highlighting the limits of presidential influence over entrenched regional adversaries. The situation demonstrates how quickly localized conflicts can spiral beyond any single actor's control.

items.headline: China Dominates African AI Development Through Local Language Models
items.summary: Chinese AI systems have become the predominant choice for African developers by offering models literate in local African languages, giving Beijing significant technological influence across the continent. This linguistic advantage represents a strategic soft power tool that Western competitors have largely overlooked. The development signals China's comprehensive approach to digital infrastructure expansion in emerging markets.

items.headline: Distributed Supply Chains Evade Detection Despite Advanced Port Security
items.summary: New scanning technology at Beirut's port successfully identified individual components like lithium batteries and drone parts but missed the threat when militants spread purchases across multiple containers, vessels, and timeframes. The case illustrates how modern AI-powered security systems struggle with threats distributed across extended supply networks rather than concentrated in single shipments. This vulnerability has implications for ports worldwide relying on similar detection methods.

items.headline: Washington Urged to Compete Rather Than Exclude China in Latin America
items.summary: U.S. strategy toward Chinese influence in Latin America should focus on offering better alternatives rather than attempting to push Beijing out entirely, according to new analysis of regional dynamics. The approach recognizes that exclusionary tactics have proven ineffective while countries in the region benefit from Chinese investment and trade relationships. Success requires Washington to provide more attractive strategic partnerships rather than demanding zero-sum choices.

sections.title: Military
sections.intro: Military operations intensify in the Gulf of Oman while Congress advances AI modernization and extends legacy platform lifespans amid ongoing security challenges.

items.headline: Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet disables oil tanker in Gulf of Oman strike
items.summary: A carrier-based F/A-18 from USS Abraham Lincoln fired precision munitions into a vessel's engineering and steering compartments in the Gulf of Oman. The strike represents escalating military action in critical maritime shipping lanes. This follows recent Iranian attacks on Kuwait, indicating broader regional tensions.

items.headline: Trump administration accelerates AI integration across national security agencies
items.summary: New presidential directive orders FBI and intelligence agencies to build "deep, proactive" partnerships with frontier AI companies. The memo signals aggressive push to modernize defense capabilities amid global AI competition. Implementation speed will test agencies' ability to balance innovation with security protocols.

items.headline: Congress extends A-10 Warthog operations through 2030 with AI upgrade studies
items.summary: House panel approved keeping the aging close-air-support aircraft operational beyond planned retirement while exploring AI and electronic warfare capabilities. Lawmakers question whether new mission profiles could justify continued investment in the platform. Decision reflects broader tension between modernization costs and proven capabilities.

items.headline: Navy sailor charged with financing ISIS attack plan against US troops
items.summary: Seaman Bareen Dzayee allegedly attempted to pay ISIS operatives to conduct drone and RPG attacks on American service members overseas. The case highlights ongoing insider threat challenges within military ranks. Separately, Navy investigators are examining a fatal shooting aboard USS John F. Kennedy with one sailor in custody.

sections.title: Intel / OSINT
sections.intro: Today's intelligence landscape shows significant geopolitical shifts with Armenia's pro-Western electoral victory despite Russian disinformation efforts, while new surveillance footage highlights evolving NATO counter-drone operations.

items.headline: Armenia's Pro-Western Government Survives Russian Information Warfare Campaign
items.summary: Prime Minister Pashinyan's Civil Contract party secured nearly 50% of votes in Sunday's election, decisively defeating the pro-Russian Strong Armenia party backed by billionaire Samvel Karapetyan. The victory demonstrates resilience against Moscow's disinformation operations as Armenia continues its pivot toward European integration. This outcome likely intensifies Russia's concerns about losing influence in the South Caucasus.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: First Combat Footage Shows NATO Fighter Engaging Drone Over Baltic Sea
items.summary: Video evidence captures a French Rafale fighter intercepting and destroying an unidentified drone during Baltic air policing operations. This appears to be the first documented aerial engagement of this type in European airspace, highlighting the growing challenge unmanned systems pose to traditional air defense. The incident underscores NATO's evolving counter-drone tactics in contested airspace.

items.headline: UK Mandates Technical Child Protection Controls on Consumer Devices
items.summary: The British government has given technology companies three months to implement built-in detection and blocking capabilities for nude images of children on smartphones and tablets. This regulatory mandate represents a significant shift toward mandatory technical safeguards rather than voluntary compliance. The requirement will test the industry's ability to deploy effective content filtering without compromising user privacy or device performance.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

sections.title: ICS / SCADA / OT
sections.intro: Industrial cybersecurity advances through AI integration while regulatory focus intensifies on critical infrastructure protection.

items.headline: Honeywell Launches AI-Enhanced OT Cybersecurity Suite for Industrial Protection
items.summary: Honeywell expanded its Operational Technology Cybersecurity Suite with AI-powered threat detection capabilities designed for industrial environments. The enhancement represents a significant step toward proactive OT security as industrial control systems face increasing cyber threats. Organizations should evaluate how AI-driven OT security tools can strengthen their operational resilience.

items.headline: Dragos Partners with Anthropic to Test AI Vulnerability Discovery in OT Security Software
items.summary: Industrial cybersecurity firm Dragos joined Anthropic's Project Glasswing to apply Claude Mythos Preview AI model for discovering vulnerabilities in its own OT security products. This collaboration demonstrates how AI can be leveraged to identify weaknesses in industrial security tools themselves. The initiative highlights the dual-edged nature of AI in OT security - both as a defensive tool and potential attack vector.

items.headline: White House Issues AI Security Strategy Targeting Critical Infrastructure Defense
items.summary: The White House released a comprehensive AI security strategy emphasizing frontier models, cyber defense, and critical infrastructure protection. This policy development follows recent executive orders strengthening cybersecurity requirements for both government and private sector entities. Critical infrastructure operators should prepare for enhanced regulatory scrutiny and compliance requirements around AI integration in OT environments.

items.headline: Congressional Hearing Examines AI's Role in Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity
items.summary: The House Homeland Security Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection conducted hearings on frontier AI applications for cyber defense and critical infrastructure resilience. The hearing reflects growing legislative interest in how advanced AI capabilities can both protect and potentially threaten industrial systems. Expect increased congressional oversight of AI deployment in critical infrastructure sectors.
